_what: Every geometric constant used to read Figure 1, measured from the raster rather than assumed.
raster: already extracted; see a previous run

map_edge_separation.interior_below_threshold_note: Pale cells and the boundaries between them. A cell at value ~0 is white on a red-white-blue map and is indistinguishable from the page by any whiteness test.
map_edge_separation.separation_note: The strongest non-map column left of the map reaches 13/209 rows (the panel letter 'a'); the map's own outer columns reach 202 and 209.

fig1a.n_ambiguous_note: Structural, not a defect: on a CONTINUOUS ramp adjacent LUT entries differ by ~2 RGB units, so almost every cell has a second swatch within 10. heatmap.match reports this and does not raise on it; what it raises on is an exact tie, and the dedupe above removes those legitimately.
fig1a.white_point_check: The diverging map's white point must be the value its middle label names, 0. Measured +0.0094, i.e. 0.47% of the half-range. The figure never prints this and draws no tick for it, so it is external to the calibration it validates.
fig1a.saturation_note: The brightest cell's RGB equals the colorbar's top interior colour and the darkest equals its bottom interior colour, so the data SPAN the scale exactly: the colour limits were set to the data's own min and max. Nothing is clipped, so no cell is a bound and value_is_bound stays empty on this panel.

fig1c.zero_prediction_note: THE UNPRINTED CHECK. The axis is calibrated on the ticks for 3, 2 and 1 ONLY; the 0 tick is fused with the baseline and was excluded, and `forbid_target` was passed so that fitting onto the baseline would be a TypeError rather than a silent class-27 absorption. The fit then predicts where value 0 falls, and it is compared with the rule the authors actually drew.
fig1c.runs_note: 38 of 41 runs are detectable for the anchor series; the missing ones are liver bars so short that their side strokes are under the 12 px run-length floor. The windows are NOT taken from the runs -- they come from the fitted pitch -- so a missing run costs nothing. bars.bar_top then refuses on those windows, which is the correct outcome and is recorded as a refusal, not a zero.

refusals.AT3-c-9CRA|liver: bar_top: detected row 1504 is within 3 px of the baseline 1507. The first scanned row is already the axis rule, so this is the baseline being read as a bar of zero height, not a measurement. Narrow y_top/y_bot to exclude the axis.
refusals.AT3-c-9CRA|spleen: bar_top: full-width rule fired at row 1504 but the right 6px flank has no covered row at all. A bar's top rule spans the full width, so it is present in both flanks; something present only in the middle is a replicate dot cluster, a whisker cap or a mean marker. That is error class 32 (F-018, F-020).
refusals.AT3-c-Bex|liver: bar_top: detected row 1504 is within 3 px of the baseline 1507. The first scanned row is already the axis rule, so this is the baseline being read as a bar of zero height, not a measurement. Narrow y_top/y_bot to exclude the axis.
refusals.AT3-c-Bex|spleen: bar_top: detected row 1505 is within 3 px of the baseline 1507. The first scanned row is already the axis rule, so this is the baseline being read as a bar of zero height, not a measurement. Narrow y_top/y_bot to exclude the axis.
refusals.AT4-c-13CRA|spleen: bar_top: no row in [1205,1508) reaches 0.90 coverage of the full 19px bar for 3 contiguous rows.

fig1c.bound_note: A bar whose entire body lies within FLOOR_PX of the drawn baseline is recorded with value_is_bound = 'upper' at the floor value, not as a zero and not as a missing value. bars.bar_top refuses on them, and that refusal is correct: 'the bar has no resolvable height' is a different statement from 'the bar is this tall'.
